residents.name: Scholar HeadA
residents.role: Head and Neck Anatomy Fellow (示意)
lines: Welcome to Head and Neck! Here we master 28 facial, mastication, and neck muscles & nerves.

Grouping 1 - Superficial Facial Expression (CN VII Facial nerve): Orbicularis oculi (closes eyelids), Orbicularis oris (compresses/protrudes lips), Nasalis (opens/closes nostrils), Buccinator (builds cheek structure, controls food)

Grouping 2 - Deep Mastication (CN V Trigeminal nerve): Temporalis (elevates/retracts mandible), Masseter (elevates/protrudes mandible from zygomatic arch), Lateral pterygoid (protrudes/depresses mandible, contralateral deviation), Medial pterygoid (elevates/protrudes mandible, contralateral deviation)

Remember our regional goal: Accurately identify the Origin, Insertion, Unilateral vs. Bilateral Action, and Cranial/Cervical Nerve Innervation of all 28 Head and Neck muscles through RPG monster quizzes.

residents.name: Therapist NeckB
residents.role: Head and Neck Kinesiology Guide (示意)
lines: Grouping 3 - Superficial, Suprahyoid & Infrahyoid Neck: Platysma (CN VII), Sternocleidomastoid (manubrium/clavicle to mastoid process, CN XI, contralateral rotation & ipsilateral lateral flexion), Digastric/Mylohyoid/Geniohyoid/Stylohyoid (elevate hyoid & depress mandible), Omohyoid/Sternothyroid/Thyrohyoid (depress/stabilize hyoid & larynx via Ansa cervicalis & C1)

Grouping 4 - Deep Prevertebral, Scalenes & Suboccipital: Longus capitis/Longus colli/Rectus capitis anterior & lateralis (head/neck flexion), Scalene anterior/medius/posterior (C2-C7 TP to 1st/2nd ribs, elevate ribs & ipsilateral neck flexion), Rectus capitis posterior major/minor & Obliquus capitis inferior/superior (C1-C2 to occiput, Suboccipital nerve, head extension & ipsilateral rotation)
Have you inspected the 3D muscle cards for Orbicularis oculi and Orbicularis oris yet?
Speak with Guardian Cranialia by the landmark when you're ready to challenge Cranial Nexus Golem!

residents.name: Scholar ShoulderA
lines: Welcome to Shoulder! Here we conquer 17 pectoral, rotator cuff, and scapular muscles.

Grouping 1 - Pectoral Region: Pectoralis major (clavicular & sternocostal heads to lateral lip of bicipital groove, adducts/medially rotates/flexes humerus, Lateral & medial pectoral nerves), Pectoralis minor (ribs 3-5 to coracoid process, protracts/depresses scapula), Serratus anterior (ribs 1-9 to medial border of scapula, protracts/upwardly rotates scapula, Long thoracic nerve), Subclavius (1st rib to clavicle, Subclavian nerve)

Grouping 2 - Rotator Cuff (SITS): Supraspinatus (supraspinous fossa to greater tubercle, abducts humerus, Suprascapular nerve), Infraspinatus (infraspinous fossa to greater tubercle, lateral rotation, Suprascapular nerve), Teres minor (lateral border of scapula to greater tubercle, lateral rotation, Axillary nerve), Subscapularis (subscapular fossa to lesser tubercle, medial rotation, Upper & lower subscapular nerves)
Remember our regional goal: Differentiate the Origin, Insertion, Scapular vs. Glenohumeral Action, and Innervation of all 17 Shoulder and Rotator Cuff muscles in English quiz battles.

residents.name: Therapist ShoulderB
lines: Grouping 3 - Glenohumeral: Deltoid (clavicle/acromion/spine of scapula to deltoid tuberosity, flexion/abduction/extension of humerus, Axillary nerve), Teres major (inferior angle of scapula to medial lip of bicipital groove, adducts/extends/medially rotates humerus, Lower subscapular nerve)

Grouping 4 - Superficial Back & Shoulder Girdle: Trapezius Upper/Middle/Lower fibers (occiput/C7-T12 to clavicle/acromion/scapular spine, elevation/retraction/depression/upward rotation, CN XI Accessory nerve), Latissimus dorsi (T7-T12/iliac crest/ribs 9-12 to floor of bicipital groove, Thoracodorsal nerve), Rhomboid minor & major (C7-T5 to medial border of scapula, retraction & downward rotation, Dorsal scapular nerve), Levator scapulae (C1-C4 TP to superior angle of scapula, elevates/downwardly rotates scapula)
Have you inspected the 3D muscle cards for Pectoralis major and Pectoralis minor yet?
Speak with Captain Glenoid by the landmark when you're ready to challenge Rotator Cuff Titan!

residents.name: Scholar ElbowA

long head: supraglenoid tubercle to radial tuberosity, flexes & supinates forearm), Brachialis (distal 1/2 anterior humerus to ulnar coronoid process/tuberosity, flexes elbow in all positions)
Remember our regional goal: Master the exact Origin, Insertion, Elbow/Radioulnar Action, and Innervation of all 9 Elbow and Forearm rotation muscles through interactive challenges.

Lateral 1/2 Anterior interosseous nerve to distal phalanges #2-5), Flexor pollicis longus (Anterior interosseous nerve to thumb distal phalanx)

npc.name: Guardian Cranialia
npc.title: Gatekeeper of Cranio-Cervical Anatomy (示意)
npc.monsterTitle: Boss of the 28 Facial, Mastication & Neck Muscles (示意)
story: Welcome to Head and Neck Island! Here, 28 intricate muscles govern facial expression, mastication, swallowing, and head posture.

Superficial facial muscles like Orbicularis oculi, Orbicularis oris, Nasalis, and Buccinator are powered by Cranial Nerve VII (Facial nerve), while deep mastication muscles—Temporalis, Masseter, and the Pterygoids—obey Cranial Nerve V (Trigeminal nerve).

In the neck, Sternocleidomastoid (CN XI) rotates the head contralaterally, Suprahyoid and Infrahyoid muscles coordinate the hyoid and larynx, and Scalenes and Suboccipital muscles control deep cervical mechanics.
npc.hint: Focus on distinguishing CN VII (Facial expression) from CN V (Mastication), remember Sternocleidomastoid's unilateral contralateral rotation (CN XI), and watch how Obliquus capitis inferior connects C2 to C1!

muscles.name: Orbicularis oculi
muscles.origin: Orbital part: Medial part of orbital margin; Palpebral part: Medial palpebral ligament; Lacrimal part: Lacrimal bone
muscles.insertion: Skin surrounding the orbit; Lateral palpebral raphe; Upper and lower eyelids
muscles.action: Closure of eyelids

muscles.name: Orbicularis oris
muscles.origin: Medial maxilla and mandible; Deep surface of peri-oral skin; Angle of mouth
muscles.insertion: Skin and fascia of the lips
muscles.action: Compression of lips; Protrusion of lips

muscles.name: Nasalis
muscles.origin: Lateral to the nasal notch of maxilla
muscles.insertion: Midline aponeurosis at the bridge of the nose
muscles.action: Opens and closes nostrils

muscles.name: Buccinator
muscles.origin: Buccinator ridge of mandible; Alveolar process of maxilla; Pterygomandibular raphe
muscles.insertion: Angle of the mouth and lateral portion of the upper and lower lips
muscles.action: Builds muscular substructure of cheeks; Controls food synergistically with tongue; Draws mouth unilaterally

muscles.name: Temporalis
muscles.origin: Temporal fossa; Temporal fascia
muscles.insertion: Ramus and coronoid process of mandible
muscles.action: Unilateral: Lateral deviation of mandible (ipsilateral); Bilateral: Elevation of mandible, Retraction of mandible

muscles.name: Masseter
muscles.origin: Zygomatic arch
muscles.insertion: Angle and lateral surface of ramus of mandible
muscles.action: Unilateral: Lateral deviation of mandible (ipsilateral); Bilateral: Elevation of mandible, Protrusion of mandible

muscles.name: Lateral pterygoid
muscles.origin: Superior head: Infratemporal surface of greater wing of sphenoid; Inferior head: Lateral surface of lateral pterygoid plate
muscles.insertion: Condyle of mandible; Capsule and articular disc of TMJ
muscles.action: Unilateral: Lateral deviation of mandible (contralateral); Bilateral: Protrusion of mandible, Depression of mandible

muscles.name: Medial pterygoid
muscles.origin: Deep head: Medial surface of lateral pterygoid plate of sphenoid bone and pyramidal process of palatine bone; Superficial head: Tuberosity of maxilla
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of angle and ramus of mandible
muscles.action: Unilateral: Lateral deviation of mandible (contralateral); Bilateral: Protrusion of mandible, Elevation of mandible

muscles.name: Platysma
muscles.origin: Inferior border of the mandible and parotid fascia
muscles.insertion: Pectoral fascia overlaying pectoralis major and deltoid muscles
muscles.action: Depression of angles of mouth and mandible; Draws skin of neck superiorly when teeth are clenched

muscles.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.origin: Sternal head: Anterior surface of manubrium; Clavicular head: Medial 1/3 of clavicle
muscles.insertion: Mastoid process; Lateral part of superior nuchal line of occipital bone
muscles.action: Unilateral: Lateral flexion of head and neck (ipsilateral), Rotation of head (contralateral); Bilateral: Flexion of neck

muscles.name: Digastric
muscles.origin: Anterior belly: Digastric fossa of mandible; Posterior belly: Mastoid notch of temporal bone
muscles.insertion: Hyoid bone
muscles.action: Elevation of hyoid bone; Depression of mandible
muscles.innervation: Anterior belly: CN V (trigeminal nerve); Posterior belly: CN VII (facial nerve)

muscles.name: Mylohyoid
muscles.origin: Mylohyoid line of mandible
muscles.insertion: Body of hyoid bone; Mylohyoid raphe

story: Welcome to Shoulder Island! Our 17 muscles balance high mobility at the glenohumeral joint with dynamic stability across the scapulothoracic wall.

The Rotator Cuff (SITS)—Supraspinatus, Infraspinatus, Teres minor, and Subscapularis—stabilizes the humeral head: three insert on the greater tubercle, while only Subscapularis inserts on the lesser tubercle for medial rotation.
Meanwhile, Serratus anterior (Long thoracic nerve) holds the scapula against the ribcage, and Trapezius (CN XI), Rhomboids (Dorsal scapular nerve), and Pectoralis minor orchestrate scapular motion.
npc.hint: Remember the bicipital groove insertions (Pectoralis major on lateral lip, Latissimus dorsi on floor, Teres major on medial lip) and that Subscapularis inserts on the lesser tubercle!

In the anterior arm, Biceps brachii, Brachialis, and Coracobrachialis are supplied by the Musculocutaneous nerve. Posteriorly, Triceps brachii and Anconeus extend the elbow via the Radial nerve.

points: Grouping 1 - Anterior Forearm Flexors: Flexor carpi radialis, Palmaris longus, Flexor digitorum superficialis (Median nerve), Flexor carpi ulnaris (Ulnar nerve), Flexor digitorum profundus (Medial 1/2 Ulnar nerve
Lateral 1/2 Anterior interosseous nerve to distal phalanges #2-5), Flexor pollicis longus (Anterior interosseous nerve to thumb distal phalanx)

Grouping 4 - Intrinsic Short Palmar & Dorsal: Lumbricals #1+2 (Median nerve) & #3+4 (Deep ulnar nerve, flex MCP & extend IP joints from FDP tendons), Palmar interossei #1-3 (adduct fingers PAD, Deep ulnar nerve), Dorsal interossei #1-4 (abduct fingers DAB, Deep ulnar nerve), Adductor pollicis (Deep ulnar nerve), Palmaris brevis (Superficial ulnar nerve)

npc.name: Artisan Carpalis
npc.title: Gatekeeper of the Wrist & Intrinsic Hand (示意)
npc.monsterTitle: Boss of the 27 Forearm & Hand Muscles (示意)
story: Welcome to Wrist and Hands Island! Here 27 muscles coordinate everything from powerful grip to delicate thumb opposition.
Anterior forearm flexors mainly follow the Median and Anterior Interosseous nerves—except Flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial half of Flexor digitorum profundus, which follow the Ulnar nerve.

Posterior forearm extensors are supplied by the Radial and Posterior Interosseous nerves. Inside the hand, the Recurrent branch of the Median nerve powers the Thenar trio, while the Deep branch of the Ulnar nerve commands Hypothenar, Interossei (PAD/DAB), Lumbricals #3-4, and Adductor pollicis!
npc.hint: Remember PAD (Palmar interossei Adduct) and DAB (Dorsal interossei Abduct), FDS (middle phalanges/PIP) vs. FDP (distal phalanges/DIP), and that Adductor pollicis is innervated by the Deep branch of the ulnar nerve!

Grouping 4 - Pelvic Floor & Perineum: Levator ani (Puborectalis, Pubococcygeus, Iliococcygeus) & Coccygeus (pelvic floor elevation & visceral support), External anal sphincter, Superficial & Deep transverse perinei, Ischiocavernosus, Bulbospongiosus (Perineal & inferior rectal nerves)

npc.title: Gatekeeper of the Axial Spine & Core (示意)
npc.monsterTitle: Boss of the 26 Back, Abdominal & Pelvic Muscles (示意)
story: Stand tall on Trunk Island! Our 26 muscles form the axial pillar of the human body, spanning extrinsic and intrinsic back extensors, abdominal walls, the respiratory diaphragm, and the pelvic floor.
Deep intrinsic back muscles like Erector spinae, Semispinalis, Multifidus, and Rotatores are innervated by posterior rami of spinal nerves to extend, rotate, and stabilize the vertebral segments.

Anteriorly, External obliques rotate the trunk contralaterally while Internal obliques rotate ipsilaterally; the Diaphragm drives inspiration via the Phrenic nerve; and Levator ani supports the pelvic floor.
npc.hint: Compare External obliques (contralateral rotation) vs. Internal obliques (ipsilateral rotation), Multifidus (spans 2-4 vertebrae), and the Diaphragm inserting into the Central tendon (Phrenic nerve)!

npc.name: Ranger Acetabulum
npc.title: Gatekeeper of the Pelvis & Hip Joint (示意)
npc.monsterTitle: Boss of the 17 Iliopsoas, Gluteal & Adductor Muscles (示意)
story: Welcome to Hip Island! Here 17 powerful muscles link the axial pelvis to the lower extremity across four functional groups.

Anteriorly, Iliacus and Psoas major insert on the lesser trochanter as the primary hip flexors. Posteriorly, Gluteus maximus extends and laterally rotates the hip (Inferior gluteal nerve), while Gluteus medius and minimus abduct the femur and keep the pelvis level (Superior gluteal nerve).

Deep external rotators (Piriformis, Gemelli, Obturator internus, Quadratus femoris) laterally rotate the extended hip and abduct the flexed hip, while the Medial compartment adducts the thigh via the Obturator nerve.
npc.hint: Distinguish Superior gluteal nerve (Gluteus medius, minimus, TFL) from Inferior gluteal nerve (Gluteus maximus), and remember the dual innervation of Adductor magnus!

story: Welcome to Knee Island! Though only 9 muscles reside here, they include the body's most powerful extensors and biarticular stabilizers.

Anteriorly, the Quadriceps (Rectus femoris, Vastus medialis, Vastus intermedius, Vastus lateralis) and Sartorius are all innervated by the Femoral nerve; only Rectus femoris and Sartorius cross both the hip and knee.

Posteriorly, the Hamstrings—Semitendinosus, Semimembranosus, and Biceps femoris—extend the hip and flex the knee, while deep in the posterior knee, Popliteus rotates the femur laterally on a planted tibia to unlock the knee!

islands.name: Ankle and Foot
islands.intro: Explore 24 crural compartments and intrinsic foot muscles.
points: Grouping 1 - Anterior & Lateral Leg: Tibialis anterior (dorsiflexion & inversion), Extensor hallucis longus, Extensor digitorum longus, Fibularis tertius (dorsiflexion & eversion, all Deep fibular nerve), Fibularis longus & Fibularis brevis (plantarflexion & eversion, Superficial fibular nerve)

Grouping 2 - Superficial & Deep Posterior Leg (Tibial nerve): Gastrocnemius, Soleus, Plantaris (insert on calcaneus via calcaneal tendon, plantarflexion), Tibialis posterior (plantarflexion & inversion, arch support), Flexor digitorum longus, Flexor hallucis longus
Grouping 3 - Dorsal Foot (Deep fibular nerve): Extensor digitorum brevis, Extensor hallucis brevis

Grouping 4 - Intrinsic Sole of Foot (Layers 1-4): Layer 1 - Abductor hallucis & Flexor digitorum brevis (Medial plantar nerve), Abductor digiti minimi (Lateral plantar nerve), Layer 2 - Quadratus plantae (Lateral plantar nerve) & Lumbricals #1-4 (#1 Medial plantar, #2-4 Lateral plantar), Layer 3 - Flexor hallucis brevis (Medial plantar), Adductor hallucis & Flexor digiti minimi brevis (Lateral plantar), Layer 4 - Plantar interossei #1-3 (adduct digits 3-5) & Dorsal interossei #1-4 (abduct digits 2-4, Lateral plantar nerve)
RPG Quiz Directives: Challenge players in English on ankle dorsiflexors vs. plantarflexors, invertors vs. evertors, plantar foot layers 1-4, and Medial vs. Lateral plantar nerve supply
islands.extra: Differentiate the Origin, Insertion, Compartment/Layer Action, and Fibular/Tibial/Plantar Innervation of all 24 Ankle and Foot muscles.

npc.name: Navigator Talus
npc.title: Gatekeeper of the Crural Compartments & Foot Arches (示意)
npc.monsterTitle: Boss of the 24 Leg & Intrinsic Foot Muscles (示意)
story: Ahoy, traveler! You have reached Ankle and Foot Island, the foundation of human locomotion with 24 muscles across the leg compartments and four plantar foot layers.

In the leg: the Anterior compartment dorsiflexes the ankle via the Deep fibular nerve; the Lateral compartment (Fibularis longus & brevis) everts and plantarflexes via the Superficial fibular nerve; and the Superficial & Deep Posterior compartments plantarflex and invert via the Tibial nerve.

In the sole of the foot, four intrinsic muscle layers support the arches and control the digits, divided between the Medial plantar nerve (Abductor hallucis, Flexor digitorum brevis, Flexor hallucis brevis, Lumbrical #1) and the Lateral plantar nerve (all remaining plantar muscles)!
npc.hint: Remember the 4 muscles of the Medial plantar nerve (Abductor hallucis, Flexor digitorum brevis, Flexor hallucis brevis, Lumbrical #1) vs. Lateral plantar nerve, and compare Tibialis anterior vs. Tibialis posterior!
